reason: Prioritize active panel32 changes with plausible gains and bounded scope. The two K schedules preserve FP32 update order and test whether load placement or pointer work can overlap FMOPA; neither has direct active-path measurements. Packing one B panel at a time is ahead of a full 1 MiB B layout because it limits added storage and packing work while testing contiguous consumption. Prefetch is lower because the supplied distance-4 test on the inactive path regressed, though that result does not settle this active-path variant. Counter fusion is a small, low-risk test. Transpose fusion and direct A packing may reduce data movement, but their integration with the existing consumer is underspecified; the n=512 panel32 path already packs A directly, so the fallback-only transpose change does not address its timed workload. Scratch microblocking adds loop work without reducing packing, and 192-byte A padding increases footprint without evidence of cache conflicts.
